subject.title: [Bug] Cron Job 使用错误的飞书账号发送消息 - 缺少 accountId 自动推断

question: For cron delivery without `delivery.accountId`, should a configured agent/channel binding outrank a same-channel session `lastAccountId`, or should current session-first behavior remain the compatibility default?
rationale: The current code and tests intentionally preserve session-first behavior, but the report shows that behavior can cross account/security boundaries in scheduled non-interactive delivery.

options.title: Adopt binding-aware precedence
options.body: Use explicit cron account first, then a unique configured agent/channel binding, then only safe session/default fallbacks, with fail-closed tests for ambiguous bindings.

options.title: Keep session-first compatibility
options.body: Leave `lastAccountId` precedence intact and document that multi-account cron jobs must set `--account` or a stored delivery context explicitly.

options.title: Fail closed on disagreement
options.body: When a cron delivery binding and session-derived account disagree, refuse delivery and surface a clear diagnostic instead of choosing either account.

recommendation.title: Adopt binding-aware precedence
recommendation.body: Use explicit cron account first, then a unique configured agent/channel binding, then only safe session/default fallbacks, with fail-closed tests for ambiguous bindings.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame for the cron delivery resolver and its account precedence tests points there, making this the best available code-history routing candidate.
